newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian corn importers sweat as buyers sit tight.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian corn importers sweat as buyers sit tight.

text.p: Malaysian corn importers were growing increasingly anxious on Tuesday, as buyers sat tight in a market overfilled with maize, trade sources said.
A new arrival of around 70,000 tonnes of corn in the last week added to a stockpile of nearly 150,000 tonnes in the market, said the sources.
But the swell in supply did not push prices down. Bulk corn, ex-factories/godowns in Malaysia's central region, was retained at 380 to 385 ringgit per tonne C & F this week, they said.
"I think importers know that if they start quoting lower every day, they'll lose their pants faster than they can zip it up," said the purchasing manager of a flour mill in Kuala Lumpur.
But another flour mill official said it would be impossible to retain prices at the current level if the stock situation did not ease.
"I think the price could go down to 340 (ringgit) over the next month," said the official.
"Everyone is sweating, looking for buyers and even paying for warehouse space. If I'm offering at 360 a tonne, there'll be someone undercutting me at 355," added the official.
A shipping source said a major price war could still be averted if corn importers reschedule part of their consignments due over the next month.
"The stock will ease as animal feed will have to be produced daily," said a feedmill official. "But the question is how long?"
Prices of other grains were stable.
"A" grade wheat in bags was unchanged at 730 ringgit. "B" grade wheat was steady at 430 ringgit.
Soymeal was maintained at 880 ringgit for the local material and 870 for the imported stuff. .
